method: All inputs are read in the browser and nothing is sent anywhere. For source resistance Rs and load resistance Rl, one L-section has its loaded Q fixed by the resistance ratio: Q = sqrt(Rhigh / Rlow - 1), where Rhigh and Rlow are the larger and smaller of the two resistances. The series reactance Xs = Q x Rlow sits in line with the smaller resistance and the shunt reactance Xp = Rhigh / Q sits across the larger one. At frequency f, L = X / (2 pi f) and C = 1 / (2 pi f X). The low-pass form is a series inductor with a shunt capacitor; the high-pass form is a series capacitor with a shunt inductor. Bandwidth is the approximation f / Q. Accepted ranges: both resistances 0.5 to 10,000 ohms, a resistance ratio of at most 1,000 : 1, and frequency 0.01 to 40,000 MHz. Equal resistances are reported as already matched with no network. The calculator assumes ideal lossless components at a single frequency: it does not model component Q, tolerances, parasitics or baluns, and it does not verify power handling, voltage stress or spectrum limits.
